pamphlet_excerpts: Life and Times of Lord: The divide between rich and poor was widening, and most families were poor or close (p. 9).
Life and Times of Lord Principle 2: As people migrated to dirty, overcrowded cities, they were more likely to become sick and less likely to be able to enjoy nature or get physical exercise (p. 9).
Life and Times of Lord Principle 3: In fact, when Britain went to war in 1899, more than half the men who volunteered for the army weren't fit enough to fight (p. 9).
Life and Times of Lord Principle 4: Children on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean suffered right along with their parents (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Life and Times of Lord): Beyond the YMCA and some church-based programs, few organized activities or sports leagues were available for them to enjoy (p. 9).
Step 2 (Life and Times of Lord): Even worse, at least 1.7 million American children under the age of 16 worked full time, sometimes working as many as 12 hours a day in factories (p. 9).
Step 3 (Life and Times of Lord): Many adults grew deeply concerned about the problems of English and Child laborer, circa early 20th century American children (p. 9).
Step 4 (Life and Times of Lord): Among them were Robert Baden-Powell, Ernest Thompson Seton, and Daniel Carter Beard (p. 9).

quiz_item.question: What historic event did Lord Robert Baden-Powell organize in August 1907 on Brownsea Island in Poole Harbour, England, and what did it lead to in 1908?
options: A. He convened the first World Scout Jamboree with 50,000 Scouts from thirty nations and founded the Order of the Arrow.
B. He wrote the United States congressional charter for the Boy Scouts of America alongside William D. Boyce and Ernest Thompson Seton.
C. He established the Philmont Scout Ranch in New Mexico and published the first American Scout Handbook.
D. He held an experimental camp with 20 boys from diverse social backgrounds organized into four patrols to test his outdoor training ideas, which led to publishing Scouting for Boys in 1908.

pamphlet_excerpts: Scouting's Programs Have Developed: In 1935, the BSA created a program called Explorer Scouts asone option in Senior Scouting (p. 38).
Scouting's Programs Have Developed Principle 2: It offered to older Boy Scouts a land-based alternative to Sea Scouting (p. 38).
Scouting's Programs Have Developed Principle 3: Explorer Scouts initially wore the same uniform as Boy Scouts, although it featured an "Explorer Scout, BSA" strip over the right pocket (p. 38).
Scouting's Programs Have Developed Principle 4: In the 1940s, a forest-green uniform was introduced, and Explorer Scout units began to be called posts instead of troops (p. 38).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): Explorer Scouts got their own advancement program in 1944 (p. 38).
Step 2 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): The four ranks, Apprentice, Woodsman, Frontiersman, and Ranger, corresponded to the four ranks in Sea Scouting (p. 38).
Step 3 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): In 1949, Explorer Scouts became simply Explorers, and the program's focus was expanded to include social activities, service opportunities (p. 38).
Step 4 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): More and more, posts began to specialize in specific careers or hobbies (p. 38).
